analysis: The changes are documentation-only: a date bump and a new eviction-order paragraph in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, and a new 'Active-store victim selection' row in the eviction table of docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (around line 375). No executable code, key handling, crypto, TTL, disk-budget values or routing logic changed in the supplied units. The unit f9236a49870eace9:7 is prefix-cache.md lines 858-969. It covers the invariants, failure modes and code map and shows no new text there; the new eviction paragraph near line 531 is only in the patch excerpt. I checked it against T-041 and the SEC-035 posture. The docs describe LRU victim selection as a linear probe, then a heap snapshot taken after the first attempt, ordered by last hit and lexicographic tag. The 30-minute sliding TTL, the default disk budget of half the free space with a 20 GiB fallback, HMAC-keyed names, and the KEK-wipe purge are unchanged. The TTL text in the reference file still cites the T-041/SEC-035 sign-off, so no threat-model assumption is invalidated. One caveat: the docs say concurrent schedules may select different victims than a pre-attempt snapshot. That affects eviction order only, not confidentiality or integrity. The retirement code (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift, SSDBlockIndex.swift) was not supplied, so I cannot verify that the described behavior (file leases, epoch validation, removal lock, external-removal reconciliation) matches the implementation. The accompanying code change, if it is in another batch, should be checked for TOCTOU or removal-lock bypass; this is an integration question rather than a finding. Also, the reference doc patch excerpt is truncated, but the base text is fully visible and the head change is a single added row.
